sentences.zh: 在你长大的地方，大家去搞艺术、当演员、上这种艺术学校是很普遍的事吗？

sentences.en: Not become an actor.
I mean, in New Orleans, you know, every little boy grows up wanting to be a trumpet player.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在新奥尔良，每个小男孩长大都想当个小号手。

sentences.en: You know, everybody wants to be a musician.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想成为音乐家。

sentences.en: Everybody wants to march in the parades.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想参加游行队伍。

sentences.en: Right, all right.
But were your parents musicians or in the arts at all?
sentences.zh: 但你父母是搞音乐或艺术的吗？

sentences.en: No, hell no.
My daddy worked.
My daddy was a roofer, you know.
So it was six of us.
He had to work.
Oh, fuck.
Roofing in New Orleans, too.
sentences.zh: 而且还是在新奥尔良修屋顶。

sentences.en: That is not.
Yeah, my mom was a homemaker, and my dad was a roofer.
sentences.zh: 我妈是家庭主妇，我爸是修屋顶的。

sentences.en: So it, but they always stressed on us education and going to school.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们一直强调教育和上学的重要性。

sentences.en: So it was very important to them that we did something that fulfilled our dreams and kept us interested.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，我们能做些实现梦想且感兴趣的事情非常重要。

sentences.en: But also, probably, they had their eye on practicality, too.
sentences.zh: 但可能他们也考虑到了现实层面。

sentences.en: It sounds like they were not afraid of good, hard work and some pleasant predictability about income and providing.
sentences.zh: 听起来他们不怕辛苦工作，也希望收入和生活能有稳定的保障。

sentences.en: Were they sort of, you sure you want to pursue acting or the arts is something that, like, how about getting, like, a quote, unquote, real job?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有那种，你确定要追求表演或艺术吗？要不要考虑找份所谓的“正经工作”？

sentences.en: Was there pressure for you to do that as well?
sentences.zh: 你有没有感受到这方面的压力？

sentences.en: No, not at all.
My parents, my dad had one rule.
sentences.zh: 我父母，我爸就一条规矩。

sentences.en: Do whatever you want.
Be the best at it.
Just don't go to jail.
Oh, that's cool.
That was it.
Wow.
That's a good rule.
Like, you can be a damn garbage man.
sentences.zh: 就算你想去当个垃圾清理工也行。

sentences.en: Just be the best garbage man and don't go to jail.
sentences.zh: 只要做最好的垃圾清理工，别进监狱就行。

sentences.en: That's it.
Like, growing up in New Orleans in the 80s and 90s, it was such a rough city.
sentences.zh: 在八九十年代的新奥尔良长大，那真是一座混乱的城市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
It was, I mean, it was the murder capital of the world.
sentences.zh: 确实，我是说，那可是世界谋杀之都。

sentences.en: I mean, they were in a city of, you know, 700,000 people, you know, four to 500 people were getting murdered a year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时那座城市有七十万人，每年有四五百人被谋杀。

sentences.en: Jesus.
Wow.
So per square capital, we were literally the murder capital of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以按人均算，我们真的是世界谋杀之都。

sentences.en: Wow, I didn't know that.
So, yeah, it was wildly dangerous in the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，九十年代初那里极其危险。

sentences.en: Did you have brothers and sisters or were you an only child?
sentences.zh: 你有兄弟姐妹吗，还是独生子女？

sentences.en: Five of them, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我有五个兄弟姐妹，是的。

sentences.en: Wow.
Yeah.
Wow.
And, you know, we're all vastly different in very different ways.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们每个人在各方面都大不相同。

sentences.en: Anybody else go into the arts?
sentences.zh: 还有其他人从事艺术行业吗？

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no, no.
My brother, you know, was a singer, but he also played tennis.
sentences.zh: 我哥哥是个歌手，但他同时也打网球。

sentences.en: So all that shit's weird, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都很奇怪，你懂我意思吗？

sentences.en: Right, right.
So, I mean, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So you go and then you go to North Carolina, then you go up, you get into Juilliard, you go to Juilliard, and I always wondered this.
sentences.zh: 所以你去了北卡罗来纳州，然后又去了纽约，考进了茱莉亚学院，你去了茱莉亚，我一直很好奇这一点。

sentences.en: So you graduate Juilliard, you've got a degree from arguably like the premier place to get an acting degree, certainly in the States.
sentences.zh: 你从茱莉亚学院毕业，拿到了学位，这可以说是美国首屈一指的表演专业学位。

sentences.en: And is it like, okay, you know, the day after you graduate, is it like everybody's knocking at your door, or is it just hit the streets and start auditioning like everybody else?
sentences.zh: 那么，毕业后的第二天，是不是所有人都排着队来找你，还是说你得像其他人一样去街上到处试镜？

sentences.en: Well, you do this thing called league scenes, and you invite all the agents and all the agencies to come see the graduating class do their monologues.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会进行一种叫“毕业汇报演出”的东西，邀请所有的经纪人和经纪公司来看毕业班表演独白。

sentences.en: Like a showcase.
A showcase, yeah.
And everybody comes, and from that, hopefully you'll get an agent or a manager.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会来，希望通过这个机会能签到经纪人或经理人。

sentences.en: And I got lucky.
I did these, you know, three scenes, and they were fine.
sentences.zh: 我当时演了三个片段，表现还不错。

sentences.en: You know, it was cool.
But what really helped me was when I was in school, we wrote this play about Tupac called Up Against the Wind.
sentences.zh: 但真正帮到我的是，我在学校时和同学一起写了一部关于图派克的剧，叫《逆风而行》。

sentences.en: Yes.
And, you know, we all did it.
Like, you know, there was a girl, Rosemary, in a directing program, Michael in a writing program, and all of us actors.
sentences.zh: 比如，有个叫罗斯玛丽的女孩在导演系，迈克尔在编剧系，还有我们这些演员。

sentences.en: We all wrote and produced the scene ourselves, I mean, the show ourselves at school.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都在学校里自己编写并制作了那场戏。

sentences.en: So when we did the show, Jim Nicola from New York Theater Workshop came to see the show and was like, I want to move this off Broadway.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们演出时，纽约戏剧工作室的吉姆·尼古拉来看了，他说想把这部戏搬到外百老汇去演。

sentences.en: So it was a big problem at Juilliard because you're not allowed to do outside work while you're a student.
sentences.zh: 这在茱莉亚学院成了个大问题，因为学生在校期间是不允许从事校外工作的。

sentences.en: Okay.
And it came down—
But it was a gray area because you guys had started it at the school.
sentences.zh: 但这属于灰色地带，因为你们是在学校里发起的这个项目。

sentences.en: We started it at the school.
sentences.zh: 我们是在学校里发起的。

sentences.en: Right.
And, you know, it was very eye-opening because there was a fight between me and the staff if I would do this play off Broadway, which was created at the school,
sentences.zh: 那次经历让我大开眼界，因为我和校方之间产生了一场争执，关于我是否能去演这部在外百老汇上演的、但在学校创作的剧，

sentences.en: or if I would do the checkoff play for my final grade of the year.
sentences.zh: 还是说我必须去演契诃夫的剧来完成那一年的期末成绩。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
Right.
So we were going back and forth about that, and they were very adamant about not letting me do this play.
sentences.zh: 我们为此争执不下，他们非常坚持不让我去演那部戏。

sentences.en: And then the play caught fire and took off, and all of a sudden, everybody was a supporter.
sentences.zh: 后来那部戏火了，突然之间，所有人都变成了支持者。

sentences.en: Sure.
A teacher who was interviewed by the New York Times, and true story, this is still in print.
sentences.zh: 有一位老师接受了《纽约时报》的采访，这是真实的故事，现在还能查到报道。

sentences.en: She said, you know, usually the black kids just sit around and wait to see who's going to play Othello,
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，通常黑人孩子只是坐着等看谁能去演奥赛罗，

sentences.en: but it's great that they created something that they can go and do in the New York Theater.
sentences.zh: 但很高兴他们创造了一些东西，让他们可以去纽约剧院表演。

sentences.en: Whoa!
What?
Yeah.
What does that even mean?
Like, what—
Yeah, it means she was a fucking idiot.
sentences.zh: 是啊，意思是她是个彻头彻尾的白痴。

sentences.en: I know, like, what?
That's, like, crazy.
Yeah.
What?
It means she was a fucking idiot.
sentences.zh: 意思是她是个彻头彻尾的白痴。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
Wow.
That's what it means.
That must have lit a fire under your—like, a little bit to be like, like, I'm going to—yeah, like—
sentences.zh: 那一定让你深受触动，让你觉得，我一定要——是啊，就像——

sentences.en: Yeah, and that was my biggest thing, like, coming out of that school.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那是我从那所学校出来后最大的感触。

sentences.en: It was really eye-opening for many different reasons, because I went to go see a play, like, every two weeks.
sentences.zh: 那段经历让我大开眼界，原因有很多，因为我每两周就会去看一场戏。

sentences.en: Right.
And I saw so much bad theater, but I saw so much good theater.
sentences.zh: 我看了很多糟糕的戏剧，但也看了很多优秀的戏剧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
You know, and so much small theater and innovative and courageous theater.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有很多小型、创新且大胆的戏剧。

sentences.en: And it really just formed and shaped me.
What I saw really formed and shaped me more than what I learned in school.
sentences.zh: 我所看到的比我在学校学到的更能塑造我。

sentences.en: Yeah.
And now, you find yourself—sorry, Sean.
sentences.zh: 现在，你发现自己——抱歉，肖恩。

sentences.en: You find yourself at a place of great success with tons of momentum and futures wide open.
sentences.zh: 你发现自己正处于一个非常成功的阶段，势头强劲，未来无限广阔。

sentences.en: Did you allow yourself to see yourself at this place at this age, or are you kind of like—you know, it's a tough question to answer,
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过自己在这个年纪会达到这个位置，还是说你有点——你知道，这很难回答，

sentences.en: but are you where you thought you would be?
sentences.zh: 但你现在是你预想中的样子吗？

sentences.en: Are you over-performing, under-performing?
sentences.zh: 你表现得超乎预期，还是低于预期？

sentences.en: You've got to be happy.
You've got to be content.
You know, this is a weird business, and, you know, psychologically, it's a huge mindfuck to be a part of this business,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一行很奇怪，心理上来说，身处这个行业简直是一种折磨，

sentences.en: because I never thought I would be here.
sentences.zh: 因为我从没想过我会走到今天这一步。

sentences.en: Like, I never—when I got into this business, I didn't say, oh, I want to be famous, or I want to be a movie star.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有——当我进入这个行业时，我没说，哦，我想出名，或者我想成为电影明星。

sentences.en: I literally dreamed about being a working actor.
sentences.zh: 我真的只是梦想成为一名职业演员。

sentences.en: Like, I wanted to, you know, work at the Guthrie.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，在格思里剧院工作。

sentences.en: I wanted to work at Penumbra, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想在半影剧院工作，你知道的。

sentences.en: That's why you've had longevity.
sentences.zh: 这就是你能长久发展的原因。

sentences.en: And that was the focus of my career.
sentences.zh: 那是我职业生涯的重心。

sentences.en: Like, how can I do these great roles, you know, you know, these great American theater roles in great theaters around the country, you know?
sentences.zh: 比如，我怎样才能演好这些伟大的角色，你知道，在全国各地的伟大剧院里演绎这些伟大的美国戏剧角色，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And it just so happened, you know, because it sounds like such an asshole story.
sentences.zh: 结果就这么发生了，你知道，因为这听起来像个混蛋故事。

sentences.en: So when we were doing Up Against the Wind, there was this amazing casting director named Molly Finn, guy, rest of the soul.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们排演《逆风而行》时，有一位了不起的选角导演叫莫莉·芬恩，愿她安息。

sentences.en: And she was in New York.
She came to see the play.
And Curtis Hanson was putting together 8 Mile.
sentences.zh: 当时柯蒂斯·汉森正在筹备《8英里》。

sentences.en: Right.
That's right.
So she came to see the play.
I get to audition for Curtis Hanson.
sentences.zh: 我有机会去参加柯蒂斯·汉森的试镜。

sentences.en: And I was always a huge fan of Curtis from L.A.
sentences.zh: 我一直都是柯蒂斯的大粉丝，从《洛城机密》开始就是了，

sentences.en: Confidential, from all the shit he had did.
sentences.zh: 因为他拍过的那些牛逼作品。

sentences.en: And my audition—like, it was just funny.
sentences.zh: 而我的那场试镜——怎么说呢，挺逗的。

sentences.en: I always had a belief, if you get people to directing you and working with you, that's because they're interested in you.
sentences.zh: 我一直坚信，如果有人找你试镜、想和你合作，那是因为他们对你感兴趣。

sentences.en: If you audition and they go, good job, kid, thanks for coming in, then nine times out of ten, you ain't getting that job.
sentences.zh: 如果你试镜完，他们说“干得好，孩子，谢谢你过来”，那十有八九，你拿不到那个角色。

sentences.en: So I walk in and I meet Curtis, sit down.
sentences.zh: 所以我走进去见了柯蒂斯，坐了下来。

sentences.en: Curtis was a cool cat, like, love him to death.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯是个酷毙了的人，我简直爱死他了。

sentences.en: And I asked him—I said, so that was right when, like, a year after Wonder Boys had came out.
sentences.zh: 我问他——我说，那时候正好是《天才接班人》上映一年后。

sentences.en: And I said, Curtis, I have a question for you before we start.
sentences.zh: 我说，柯蒂斯，在开始之前，我有个问题想问你。

sentences.en: He's like, yeah, sure, go ahead.
So I was like, Wonder Boys.
sentences.zh: 我就提到了《天才接班人》。

sentences.en: I'm like, was that meant to be an ode to Alfred Hitchcock?
sentences.zh: 我问，那部电影是想向阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克致敬吗？

sentences.en: Or were you, like, directing it in a sense towards the ideals and teachings of Hitchcock and the way he worked?
sentences.zh: 还是说，你在导演时是有意借鉴了希区柯克的理念、教学以及他的工作方式？

sentences.en: So he goes, whoa, what are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 他听完说，哇，你在说什么呢？

sentences.en: What do you mean?
So I explained to him what I saw in the movie and, you know,
sentences.zh: 于是我向他解释了我在电影里看到的那些东西，你知道的，

sentences.en: what he did with Tobey Maguire and the backdrops in the scene and the escalating visual aspect that tied into the mental frustration of the character.
sentences.zh: 比如他如何处理托比·马奎尔的戏份，场景中的背景布置，以及那种与角色内心挫败感相呼应的视觉升级。

sentences.en: And we talked for, like, an hour about Wonder Boys.
sentences.zh: 然后我们聊了大概一个小时关于《天才接班人》的话题。

sentences.en: I never read—never did my audition.
sentences.zh: 我根本没读剧本，也没进行试镜。

sentences.en: So I come out and I'm like, fuck.
Oops.
I blew my time.
You know?
So I'm like, don't do that again.
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，下次别再这样了。

sentences.en: Don't do that again.
So three weeks later, he called and he was like, yo, cast somebody else in a role that you came in for.
sentences.zh: 结果三周后，他打来电话说，嘿，你来试镜的那个角色我已经定别人了。

sentences.en: But there's another role.
It's only four days.
If you—I don't want to offend you.
I know you're a trained actor, but if you're willing to do it, you know, I'd love to have you in Detroit.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是科班出身的演员，但如果你愿意的话，我很希望能让你来底特律拍戏。

sentences.en: So I'm like, hell yes, Curtis Hanson.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，当然愿意啊，那可是柯蒂斯·汉森。

sentences.en: So fly to Detroit and just sit with Curtis Hanson and eat dinner and, like, kick it for, like, two weeks.
sentences.zh: 于是我飞到底特律，和柯蒂斯·汉森一起吃饭，在那儿待了两周，闲聊打发时间。

sentences.en: And the role only was four scenes.
sentences.zh: 那个角色其实只有四场戏。

sentences.en: Yeah.
Right?
And he was like, you have anything booked after this?
sentences.zh: 然后他问我，你拍完这个还有别的安排吗？

sentences.en: I said, not.
He was like, well, so if I extend your role, you can stay.
sentences.zh: 他说，那好，如果我增加你的戏份，你就能留下来。

sentences.en: I'm like, fuck yeah, I can stay.
sentences.zh: 我心想，去他妈的，我当然能留下来。

sentences.en: Ain't going nowhere.
So they extended my contract to a run of picture.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把我的合同延长到了整部电影的拍摄周期。

sentences.en: And we developed that role over the course of—
sentences.zh: 我们就在那段时间里不断完善那个角色——

sentences.en: That's really cool.
And that's kind of how it started.
That's amazing.
That's so cool.
You guys kind of built it off a person, like, just like a dialogue that you were having with him about, like, a shared intereSt.
sentences.zh: 你们就像是基于一个共同的兴趣，通过对话交流，一点点把这个角色给建立起来了。

sentences.en: Like, that's so—
That's what's so funny.
In the movie, like, Eminem has that, you know, rap at the end of the movie where he's like, you went to private school and all that shit.
sentences.zh: 在电影里，阿姆（Eminem）最后那段说唱，你知道吧，他当时就说，你上的是私立学校之类的那些屁话。

sentences.en: If you go back, like, he's—we had a conversation a week before, and we're talking shit, and, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下，其实我们在一周前还聊过天，当时还在互相损对方，你知道的，

sentences.en: Eminem is just an amazing dude and a lovely human being once you spend time with him.
sentences.zh: 阿姆真的是个很棒的家伙，只要你跟他相处过，就会发现他是个可爱的人。

sentences.en: It's just funny, but he's always learning and hearing and listening.
sentences.zh: 这挺有意思的，他总是保持学习，去听、去感受。

sentences.en: Like, he's like a fucking sponge.
sentences.zh: 他就像块海绵一样，吸收能力极强。

sentences.en: So we get to set the next day, and he's like, yo, there's no reason why I don't like this dude.
sentences.zh: 所以第二天到了片场，他就说，嘿，我没理由不喜欢这家伙。

sentences.en: Like, yeah, we beefing, but nobody knows about our backstory and our history, so we need to put that in the script.
sentences.zh: 他说，虽然我们有矛盾，但没人知道我们的背景和过往，所以我们得把这些写进剧本里。

sentences.en: So Curtis was like, yeah, yeah, yeah, you write, you write.
sentences.zh: 于是柯蒂斯（Curtis）就说，行行行，你来写，你来写。

sentences.en: So it comes the battle scene, right?
sentences.zh: 然后就到了那场对决戏，对吧？

sentences.en: And I write my rhyme.
I'm like, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, right?
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，砰砰砰砰砰，一顿输出，对吧？

sentences.en: We go to set, and fucking Eminem starts his rap.
sentences.zh: 我们到了片场，结果阿姆那混蛋开始了他的说唱。

sentences.en: And he's like, you went to private school.
sentences.zh: 他唱道：你上的是私立学校。

sentences.en: I was like, I did go to private school.
sentences.zh: 我心想，我确实上过私立学校。

sentences.en: He's like, your parents have a real good marriage.
sentences.zh: 他又唱：你父母的婚姻非常美满。
